articles.title: Von der Leyen calls for EU solidarity on AI, climate and China in 2026 State of the Union address
articles.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen urged EU member states to act jointly on artificial intelligence, climate change and competition from China, warning no single nation can tackle these challenges alone.
articles.content: In her annual State of the Union address to the European Parliament in Strasbourg, von der Leyen stressed maintaining European independence in energy, raw materials and clean technologies. She acknowledged citizens' concerns that AI threatens jobs and cybersecurity, and said EU leaders must ensure Europe's economy benefits from AI. The address comes as the EU enforces its AI Act and weighs massive AI infrastructure investments through proposed gigafactories, with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in Strasbourg to deepen EU-Canada ties.

articles.title: Anthropic to open Singapore office in October, chasing OpenAI for Southeast Asia's AI market
articles.description: Anthropic will establish its first Southeast Asian office in Singapore in October 2026, accelerating competition with OpenAI which already has its Asia headquarters in the city-state.
articles.content: The move signals Anthropic's push to expand globally amid intensifying EU AI Act enforcement on its Claude models. OpenAI established its Asia headquarters in Singapore in late 2024. The expansion comes as both companies face increasing regulatory scrutiny in Europe, where the European Commission has tightened AI Act enforcement on systemic-risk models from both providers, making global diversification increasingly important for AI labs under dual regulatory pressure.

articles.title: Meta's Zuckerberg and Nvidia's Huang reject coordinated AI slowdown as Amodei and Altman call for restraint
articles.description: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said competition and liability provide sufficient incentive for AI companies to build safely, distancing himself from safety proposals from OpenAI and Anthropic leaders.
articles.content: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang joined Zuckerberg in rejecting coordinated AI development pauses. Zuckerberg revealed Meta delayed its Muse AI agent for months to focus on safety but argued every lab has individual responsibility rather than needing collective slowdown. The divide deepens the industry split between companies advocating voluntary safety pacts and those insisting market incentives are enough, a debate with direct implications for EU AI Act enforcement which relies on systemic-risk model providers self-reporting safety measures.

articles.title: Legal analysis: EU AI Act and GDPR compliance intersect through existing data governance frameworks
articles.description: A new legal analysis examines how AI system providers can leverage existing GDPR data governance practices to meet AI Act training data requirements, reducing duplicate compliance burdens.
articles.content: The analysis comes as companies face overlapping obligations under the AI Act, GDPR and the Cyber Resilience Act, with no formal coordination between the frameworks. It argues that providers of AI systems trained on personal data can satisfy AI Act transparency requirements through GDPR-compliant data governance already in place, though gaps remain for synthetic data and non-personal training sets. The findings are relevant to the EU's Digital Omnibus proposal which aims to reduce regulatory burdens across digital legislation.

articles.title: EU Kids Act draft sets 15 as minimum age for unsupervised social media, with platform pre-clearance rules
articles.description: The European Commission's draft EU Kids Act would set 15 as the age for autonomous social media accounts, require age verification, and force very large platforms to get Brussels' approval before launching new features for minors.
articles.content: The draft Communication, scheduled for presentation on September 17, defines a Social Media Plus category covering social media, video-sharing platforms, online games, AI chatbots and AI companions. It proposes four age brackets: no access under 3, parent-controlled accounts from 3 to 13, limited introductory accounts from 13 to 15, and autonomous accounts from 15 to 18. Very large platforms would face a 30-day pre-clearance window for new features. The plan still needs approval from the European Parliament and Council, with discrepancies between draft versions still unresolved.

articles.title: UK workers spend nearly one billion pounds of their own money on AI tools for work, Deloitte finds
articles.description: A landmark Deloitte survey of 25,000 UK workers reveals one in six is paying for generative AI tools out of pocket, with total annual employee spending approaching 958 million pounds.
articles.content: The research, described as the UK's largest survey of workplace AI adoption, found that employees are funding AI tools faster than employers are providing them. The findings highlight a significant shift in how AI is entering European workplaces, with workers adopting AI independently rather than waiting for corporate deployment. Deloitte warns this creates governance and data protection challenges for employers who may not know which AI tools their staff are using with company data, raising questions under UK GDPR and EU AI Act frameworks.

articles.title: Europe's push for AI sovereignty is deepening dependency on US Big Tech, analysis warns
articles.description: A Rosa-Luxemburg-Stiftung analysis argues that European policies aimed at digital sovereignty are instead increasing reliance on US technology companies for chips, cloud and AI infrastructure.
articles.content: The report examines how AI supply chains concentrate power in US firms like Google, OpenAI, Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure, which control two-thirds of the global cloud market. It warns that European investment in AI infrastructure, rather than creating independence, often integrates European economies more deeply into US technology ecosystems. The analysis challenges the narrative behind EU AI gigafactory proposals and raises questions about whether current sovereignty strategies serve European interests or primarily benefit US technology providers.

articles.description: The Midas Project accuses OpenAI of multiple violations of California's AI safety law, including failing to publish risk assessments for 'loss of control' dangers required by SB 53 for models released in the past year.
articles.content: The complaint covers the GPT-6 Astra model launch and earlier releases. California's SB 53, modelled partially on the EU AI Act's systemic-risk framework, requires developers of frontier models to publish safety assessments. The accusation adds regulatory pressure on OpenAI at a time when the EU's AI Office is also scrutinising the company's Astra model under general-purpose AI rules. OpenAI has not yet publicly responded to the specific allegations.

articles.title: Trump calls AI risk a 'hoax' as Microsoft, Google and Anthropic write their own safety rules
articles.description: President Trump dismissed AI existential risk as a 'HOAX' on Truth Social and via speakerphone at the All-In Summit, while on the same day Microsoft published a 37-page AI code of conduct and major labs discussed forming a standards body.
articles.content: Microsoft's Humanist AI Code of Conduct forbids its models from resisting shutdown and is open for six weeks of public comment. Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI have discussed an industry standards body to test frontier models before release. An Anthropic co-founder told the BBC that a verifiable 'kill switch' may need to be mandatory. The juxtaposition of presidential dismissal and industry self-regulation creates a stark contrast with the EU's statutory AI Act approach.

articles.title: Apple ships Siri AI to EU Macs but withholds it from EU iPhones at launch
articles.description: Apple launched Siri AI on September 14 as part of iOS 27 and macOS 27 Golden Gate, but EU users only get the assistant on Macs, not on iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch, due to regulatory decisions.
articles.content: Under-13 accounts get no assistant at all, and Screen Time now caps daily minutes on social apps. Siri AI launches in English first, with five additional languages arriving in October. The EU exclusion applies to iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS. The split highlights the ongoing tension between Apple's AI rollout and EU regulatory requirements under the AI Act and Digital Markets Act.

articles.title: AI safety warnings hit ASML as European semiconductor stocks fall sharply
articles.description: European semiconductor shares dropped sharply after AI executives called for slowing frontier model development, forcing investors to reassess the AI infrastructure spending cycle underpinning valuations of ASML, ASM International, Infineon, and Soitec.
articles.content: Soitec fell 12.6%, Infineon 7.6%, ASM International 8.7%, and ASML 5.2% on September 14. The sell-off matters for Europe because the continent's AI exposure lies in semiconductor infrastructure rather than consumer AI platforms. ASML had explicitly linked Q2 demand to AI investment and announced 30% capacity increases for 2027. The EU AI Act's enforcement powers over systemic-risk models, active since August 2, add a regulatory dimension to the market reassessment.

articles.title: Swedish drone detection startup Freya raises 533k euros for European expansion
articles.description: Freya Industries, a Swedish company developing intelligent sensors for security and defence, has closed an oversubscribed seed round of 533k euros to scale its team and accelerate European rollout of its drone detection technology.
articles.content: The funding comes amid growing European defence spending on counter-drone systems, driven by the war in Ukraine and NATO's eastern flank security concerns. The company is part of a growing Nordic defence tech ecosystem benefiting from both national and EU-level security investment. The round reflects strong early-stage investor appetite for dual-use AI defence technologies in Europe.

articles.title: European fintech Chift raises 10.5M euros to connect Europe's fragmented financial software
articles.description: Chift, a European financial data connectivity platform, has raised 10.5 million euros to integrate accounting and business software for SMEs across Europe's fragmented national markets.
articles.content: The round reflects growing investor interest in European fintech infrastructure plays that solve the continent's regulatory and linguistic fragmentation. Chift acts as a specialist integrator connecting accounting platforms, banking APIs, and business software across multiple EU jurisdictions. The funding will expand the platform's coverage of European accounting and ERP systems. The deal signals that European B2B fintech remains attractive despite the broader 63% decline in European tech funding in August.

articles.title: EU to propose ban on social media and AI chatbots for under-15s in sweeping Kids Act
articles.description: The European Commission will propose restricting under-15s from social media, AI chatbots, video platforms, and online games under a new EU Kids Act announced by President von der Leyen and tech chief Henna Virkkunen.
articles.content: The proposal creates age-tiered access: children 15 and over can set up their own accounts, 13-14 year olds get parental-controlled introductory accounts with strict limits, 3-12 year olds get parent-controlled child-friendly accounts, and under-3s get no access. Companies must verify ages, avoid addictive designs, provide reporting tools, and pay a supervisory fee. The announcement is expected alongside the SOTEU address on September 16.

articles.description: Former White House AI czar David Sacks told Anthropic and OpenAI to voluntarily slow frontier model development but warned against seeking antitrust waivers or government approval regimes.
articles.content: Sacks argued that product liability should discipline AI companies rather than an approval regime, a stance that contrasts with the EU's AI Act enforcement model. He noted that Europe decided in 2025 to use strict liability rules and that the US should not follow with a pre-approval system. The comments come as both companies flag extinction risks above 10%.

articles.description: Speaking at his Doonbeg golf resort in Ireland, President Trump dismissed calls from AI industry leaders to slow development, likening critics to 'very negative forces' raising exaggerated concerns.

articles.description: The European Commission has affirmed that the AI Act already governs systemic-risk AI models and is tightening enforcement checks on frontier models from OpenAI and Anthropic, including assessment of loss-of-control risks.
articles.content: The enforcement actions align with the AI Act's August 2 activation of general-purpose AI model rules. Providers of systemic-risk models must assess and mitigate risks, conduct model evaluations, report serious incidents, and maintain cybersecurity protections. The move comes amid escalating safety concerns, including Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon's resignation warning that AI could kill humans by end of decade and OpenAI's disclosed agent breakout on a German website. The Commission's approach contrasts with the US deregulatory stance under the Carolina Principles endorsed at G20.

articles.description: German company Isar Aerospace became the first commercial European space company to deliver satellites into orbit, launching its Spectrum rocket from Andoya Spaceport in Norway.
articles.content: The September 5 launch marks a milestone for European sovereign space capability, with NATO's Innovation Fund highlighting its strategic importance for Allied launch independence. articles.description: NestAI, a European AI lab for defence, is opening an R&D centre in Latvia with a 10 million euro investment and 30 new high-skilled jobs, advancing defence AI capability alongside NATO forces.
articles.content: The expansion is part of NestAI's Nordic and Baltic growth strategy, positioning Latvia as a hub for defence AI on NATO's eastern flank. articles.description: Ahead of von der Leyen's September 16 State of the Union address, critics warn her planned push for AI data centres ignores energy constraints, grid limitations, and the EU's compute gap with the US and China.
articles.content: The EU president is expected to promote the EU's AI gigafactory initiative and data centre expansion in her speech. But analysts point out that Europe has only 2 GW of AI compute capacity (5% of global total), and a single planned German data centre will draw as much electricity as 600,000 households. The contradiction between AI ambitions and energy realities is becoming a central political tension.

articles.description: Bruegel's analysis of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) finds AI placed at the centre of China's industrial strategy, with significant implications for Europe's competitiveness and sovereignty.
articles.content: The think tank identifies key areas where China's AI strategy intersects with European interests, including semiconductor supply chains, open-source model dominance, and the growing geopolitical contest over compute infrastructure. The analysis recommends that Europe focus on its strengths rather than attempting full-stack replication of China's approach.
